_comment: Example cluster policy for a PAID Databricks workspace. It is not applied by this
bundle and cannot be: Databricks Free Edition is serverless-only and exposes no
cluster-policy API, so there is no classic compute for a policy to constrain.
It is included because a cost story that stops at tagging is only half of one —
tags tell you afterwards what you spent; a policy is what stops the spending.
On a paid workspace this is deployed as a `resources.cluster_policies` entry and
referenced from each job cluster by `policy_id`.

node_type_id._comment: General-purpose only. A forecasting backtest is CPU and memory bound; nobody on this pipeline needs a GPU node, and allowing one is how a job that costs cents starts costing dollars.

autoscale.max_workers._comment: A hard ceiling, not a suggestion. Without one, a bad join in a single task can scale the cluster to the account limit before anyone sees the bill.

autotermination_minutes._comment: The single most effective cost control there is: the largest avoidable line on most Databricks bills is idle compute nobody shut down.

data_security_mode._comment: Required for Unity Catalog model registry access from a job cluster.

custom_tags.product._comment: The three FinOps dimensions are enforced here rather than trusted to each job definition. A tag that can be forgotten will be.

custom_tags.country._comment: Unset or misspelled, spend lands in an 'unattributed' bucket nobody owns. The regex is the cheapest way to make attribution mandatory.
